B_note: The field B (§0.4) is, per the brief, the sources T's turn 1 surfaced as cards (B1–B6: Evergreen Review, The Walt Disney Family Museum, Theme Park Press, BiblioCommons, eBay, Instagram·Film Aesthete) and the organic results of the second address's page that are not the archive's (B7–B11: Penguin Random House Canada, Goodreads, Google Books, eCampus @ UMass, Amazon; Evergreen Review is organic result 7 there and is B1). Each source records the address that surfaced it (surfaced_at), its kind (Overview card or organic result) and whether it uses the phrase 'secret book of Walt' (none does). The second address's own Overview cards that are not organic results there (Quill and Quire, Amazon (Korkis), YouTube·Toni Shelf Help Club, Google ×3, In These Times, YouTube·Crime City) and turns 2–3's cards at both addresses are recorded in the row (objects.T.correction, objects.T2), outside B. The archive's surfaces on the page (Medium, organic 1; secretbookofwalt.org, organic 2 and T's turn-3 card) belong to A, not B (row.field_page).
lineage_note: Fetherling's novel is one work carried by five sources (B1 review; B4, B7, B8, B10 the publisher's description in catalogue, publisher, Goodreads and bookseller copies): two lineages, the review (F1–F4) and the publisher's description (F10, F13–F16, F18–F20, with F21 the edition's details). Korkis's book: the publisher (F8, F9) and a listing (F11), one lineage. Each other source is its own lineage.
pages: saved texts and hashes in each source's 'fetched'; the page files are held in the composing workspace (not created in the repository on this build)
